title: [Linux] fontFamilyFallback: ["emoji"] picks a monochrome emoji font: family preference order is lost in SkFontMgr_fontconfig matchFamily/matchStyle
body:
### Steps to reproduce

1. On Linux x64 (engine built with fontconfig), install both a color and a monochrome emoji font. On Fedora, for example: `google-noto-color-emoji-fonts` and `google-noto-emoji-fonts`.
2. Confirm fontconfig resolves the `emoji` alias to the color font:
```
$ fc-match emoji
Noto-COLRv1.ttf: "Noto Color Emoji" "Regular"
```
3. Run the code sample I provide in that step.

### Expected results

Emoji render with the font fontconfig prefers for the `emoji` alias (Noto Color Emoji), in color, matching `fc-match emoji` and GTK apps on the same system.


### Actual results

All emoji render in black and white, using Noto Emoji (the monochrome font).

Hiding Noto Emoji from fontconfig makes them render in color, which confirms the wrong font is being chosen:

```xml
<?xml version="1.0"?>
<!DOCTYPE fontconfig SYSTEM "fonts.dtd">
<fontconfig>
  <selectfont>
    <rejectfont>
      <pattern><patelt name="family"><string>Noto Emoji</string></patelt></pattern>
    </rejectfont>
  </selectfont>
</fontconfig>
```

### Likely cause

From reading the Skia source (not yet confirmed in a debugger):

1. SkParagraph's `FontCollection::matchTypeface` resolves each requested family with `manager->matchFamily(name)` and then `set->matchStyle(style)`.
2. `SkFontMgr_fontconfig::onMatchFamily("emoji")` runs `FcConfigSubstitute`, drops weak bindings with `remove_weak`, and collects **every** installed font whose family is still in the pattern. Fontconfig's `emoji` alias (`60-generic.conf`) lists the color fonts first but also includes monochrome ones (`Noto Emoji`, `Android Emoji`). So the style set contains both Noto Color Emoji and Noto Emoji, with no ordering between them.
3. `StyleSet::matchStyle` calls `FcFontSetMatch` over that set with a pattern containing only weight, width and slant, and **no family**. The alias's preference order is lost at this point. Every candidate is Regular, so the choice falls to fontconfig's tie-breaking, which here picks Noto Emoji.

`fc-match`, and `onMatchFamilyStyle` (which calls `FcFontMatch` with the full substituted pattern), keep the family list and correctly pick the color font. Only the `matchFamily` + `matchStyle` path is affected.

This is different from #75188, which was about per-character fallback (`matchFamilyStyleCharacter`) picking Symbola. Here the requested family does cover the characters, but resolving it returns the wrong member of the alias.

A possible fix would be for `StyleSet::matchStyle` to keep the substituted family list in the pattern it passes to `FcFontSetMatch`, or for SkParagraph to resolve requested families with `matchFamilyStyle`.

Workaround: list specific color emoji families before the alias, e.g. `fontFamilyFallback: ['Noto Color Emoji', 'emoji']`, or bundle an emoji font.


### Code sample

<details open><summary>Code sample</summary>

```dart
import 'package:flutter/material.dart';

void main() => runApp(
  const MaterialApp(
    home: Scaffold(
      body: Center(
        child: Text(
          '😀🎨🧑‍🚀',
          style: TextStyle(fontSize: 64, fontFamilyFallback: ['emoji']),
        ),
      ),
    ),
  ),
);
```

</details>


### Screenshots or Video

_No response_

### Logs

_No response_

### Flutter Doctor output

Not relevant, happens across machines.

title: [widget_preview] Run previews on a device other than web
body: ### Use case Widget previews only run on web. I ran the same generated scaffold on a desktop device instead, and it was faster and lighter, and previews that touch `dart:io` work. The tool only picks a web device: https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/6f5bece78e4038fbb5c1a4a2e767db481ac72946/packages/flutter_tools/lib/src/commands/widget_preview.dart#L586-L608 The device I used is [Raccoon](https://github.com/SoFluffyOS/raccoon), a small embedder-API runner on the host, used as a custom device. I ran `.widget_preview` with `flutter run -d raccoon`, and next to it `flutter run -d web-server` with headless Chrome. Same scaffold, same five previews, debug, warm caches, three runs each: | | web | Raccoon | |---|---|---| | `flutter run` to previews visible | 31.3 / 31.9 / 33.4 s | 6.8 / 7.3 / 9.7 s | | Hot reload | 132-706 ms | 80-186 ms | | Memory | 865 MB (page, browser, GPU process) | 218-261 MB | | Idle CPU | 4.4-6.6% | 0.0-0.1% | | Preview using `dart:io` | `Unsupported operation: Platform._operatingSystem` | works | | Preview using `path_provider` | fails | works | #166431 already explains why `dart:io` and `dart:ffi` can't work on web. A native device fixes that for free. | web | Raccoon | |---|---| | | | The scaffold is nearly ready for this already. Its web-only parts sit behind conditional imports with desktop variants. One thing blocks it: `initialize()` waits on `getDevToolsUri`, https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/6f5bece78e4038fbb5c1a4a2e767db481ac72946/packages/flutter_tools/templates/widget_preview_scaffold/lib/src/widget_preview_scaffold_controller.dart.tmpl#L45-L47 and the tool sets that URI only after its own web session gets a debug connection: https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/6f5bece78e4038fbb5c1a4a2e767db481ac72946/packages/flutter_tools/lib/src/commands/widget_preview.dart#L710-L715 The docs say it plainly: "This must be called, otherwise the widget previewer will hang waiting for a DevTools URI." That's what I saw. On another device the scaffold starts, then never draws a frame until a browser opens the tool's web session. ### Proposal 1. Let `flutter widget-preview start` take a device: ```sh flutter widget-preview start --device-id macos ``` Web stays the default. 2. Answer `getDevToolsUri` from the session that actually runs the scaffold, or don't block the first frame on it. That's all the scaffold needs. Platform views (`webview_flutter`) don't have to work on every device; that part can just be hidden. Related: #159342 (previews design doc), #175767 (custom scaffolds), #195082 (custom devices on macOS and Windows, which Raccoon needs). Measured on Flutter 3.47.5 stable (engine af7e796e16), macOS 26.6.1, M1 Pro. Lines above are from `master` at 6f5bece78e. Thanks!

It gets laid out as: Before: ``` Item 0 one two three four five six seven eight nine ten eleve n twelv e ``` After: ``` Item 0 one two three four five six seven eight nine ten eleve n twe lve ``` Note the difference the line breaking of `eleven twelve`. title: [material_ui] AlertDialog with only actions has no top padding
body:
### What package does this bug report belong to?

material_ui

### What target platforms are you seeing this bug on?

Android, iOS, macOS, Linux, Windows

### Have you already upgraded your packages?

Yes

### Dependency versions

<details><summary>pubspec.lock</summary>

```lock
  material_ui:
    dependency: "direct main"
    description:
      name: material_ui
      sha256: e4031746f96c8316864d9b92bce375f1320a36ed56e166307e1e1bda9d90b4ab
      url: "https://pub.dev"
    source: hosted
    version: "1.8.0"
```

</details>

### Steps to reproduce

1. Run the code sample.
2. Tap Open.

### Expected results

Some gap above the buttons. Compose wraps the dialog in a uniform 24
([AlertDialog.kt](https://github.com/androidx/androidx/blob/androidx-main/compose/material3/material3/src/commonMain/kotlin/androidx/compose/material3/AlertDialog.kt)).
material-web gives the actions slot `padding: 16px 24px 24px`
([_dialog.scss](https://github.com/material-components/material-web/blob/main/dialog/internal/_dialog.scss)).
They differ, but neither is 0.

### Actual results

0 on M3, against 24 on the sides and bottom, so the buttons sit flush to the top edge. M2 gives 8
on all four edges instead.

The M3 default is hardcoded in `DialogTemplateM3` as `EdgeInsets.only(left: 24.0, right: 24.0,
bottom: 24.0)`, no top. Not a token, the dialog token data has no padding entries, so a fix edits
that template and regenerates.

Same shape as flutter/packages#13399: a child that can come first has no inset to fall back on. The
number needs a maintainer call, since Compose and material-web differ.

### Code sample

<details open><summary>Code sample</summary>

```dart
import 'package:flutter/widgets.dart';
import 'package:material_ui/material_ui.dart';

void main() => runApp(const MaterialApp(home: DialogPage()));

class DialogPage extends StatelessWidget {
  const DialogPage({super.key});

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) => Scaffold(
    body: Center(
      child: TextButton(
        onPressed: () => showDialog<void>(
          context: context,
          builder: (_) => AlertDialog(
            actions: <Widget>[TextButton(onPressed: () {}, child: const Text('OK'))],
          ),
        ),
        child: const Text('open'),
      ),
    ),
  );
}
```

</details>

<details><summary>Widget test</summary>

```dart
import 'package:flutter_test/flutter_test.dart';
import 'package:material_ui/material_ui.dart';

// DialogPage from the code sample above.

void main() {
  testWidgets('a dialog whose only child is its actions still has a top inset', (tester) async {
    await tester.pumpWidget(const MaterialApp(home: DialogPage()));
    await tester.tap(find.text('open'));
    await tester.pumpAndSettle();

    final actions = tester.getRect(find.byType(OverflowBar));
    final surface = tester.getRect(
      find.descendant(of: find.byType(Dialog), matching: find.byType(Material)).first,
    );

    expect(actions.top - surface.top, greaterThan(0.0)); // Fails: 0.0.
  }, variant: TargetPlatformVariant.all());
}
```

</details>

### Screenshots or Videos

None, the widget test shows it.

### Logs

<details open><summary>Logs</summary>

```console
$ flutter test
a dialog whose only child is its actions still has a top inset (variant: TargetPlatform.android)
Expected: a value greater than <0.0>
  Actual: <0.0>
```

The same on every other variant.

</details>

body:
### What package does this bug report belong to?

material_ui

### What target platforms are you seeing this bug on?

Android, iOS, macOS, Linux, Windows

### Have you already upgraded your packages?

Yes

### Dependency versions

<details><summary>pubspec.lock</summary>

```lock

    dependency: "direct main"
    description:
      name: material_ui
      sha256: e4031746f96c8316864d9b92bce375f1320a36ed56e166307e1e1bda9d90b4ab
      url: "https://pub.dev"
    source: hosted
    version: "1.8.0"
```

</details>

### Steps to reproduce

1. Run the code sample.
2. Tap Open.

### Expected results

The option sits 24 from the top, the same as from the sides. `SimpleDialog.contentPadding`'s own
doc comment names 24 as the target, it just puts the adjustment on the caller.

### Actual results

It sits 20, on M2 and M3 alike. The default `contentPadding` puts 12 at the top and
`SimpleDialogOption` adds 8, and neither one knows whether a title is above it.

`AlertDialog` had the same shape and is fixed in flutter/packages#13399, where the default top
padding becomes 24 when no icon or title sits above the content. `SimpleDialog` needs its own
change because `contentPadding` is a non-nullable parameter with a const default, so a default that
depends on `title` means changing that parameter's type.

### Code sample

[Windows][3.47.6] Null parent crash in AccessibilityBridge::CreateRemoveReparentedNodesUpdate after route dismissal
body:
### Steps to reproduce

This is an intermittent production crash on Windows, with the faulting instruction symbolized against the **exact matching official engine PDB**. It appears to be the same failure as #175041; this report adds a confirmed **Flutter 3.47.6** occurrence and the observed route-transition context.

Observed app flow:
1. Run the Windows x64 release app and play a video on a page with playback controls and transcript text.
2. Open a word-detail/translation route from that page.
3. An asynchronous translation response updates the route.
4. Dismiss/pop the word-detail route.

The recorded breadcrumbs show route push, translation response 381 ms later, and route pop 1.256 s after the push. The native crash timestamp is rounded to a whole second and falls in the same second as the pop, so it cannot establish subsecond ordering of the crash and pop. A previous media-source replacement finished roughly 43 seconds earlier.

**These are the observed preceding actions, not a deterministic standalone reproduction.** The specific assistive-technology or accessibility client, if any, is unknown. The native accessibility update path was active. We have not established which framework semantics update first made the tree inconsistent.

### Expected results

Opening and dismissing the route should not terminate the app. Accessibility updates should preserve a consistent, usable tree; an invalid update should not become an unhandled native access violation.

### Actual results

The app terminates with an unhandled read access violation at address `0x48`.

The fault is a null-parent dereference in the engine's accessibility reparenting path, confirmed by the instruction pointer, registers, matching symbols, and disassembly:

```text
Exception: EXCEPTION_ACCESS_VIOLATION_READ
Invalid read address: 0x48
Faulting module: flutter_windows.dll
Module-relative instruction pointer: 0x3c1ca
RAX at the fault: 0x0

Matching-PDB inline symbolization:
ui::AXNode::id
  third_party/accessibility/ax/ax_node.h:110
flutter::AccessibilityBridge::CreateRemoveReparentedNodesUpdate
  shell/platform/common/accessibility_bridge.cc:229

Relevant instructions:
flutter_windows.dll+0x3c1c6: mov rax, [rax+0x20]  ; load AXNode parent
flutter_windows.dll+0x3c1ca: mov eax, [rax+0x48]  ; read id through null parent
```

The source at [Flutter 3.47.6](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/3.47.6/engine/src/flutter/shell/platform/common/accessibility_bridge.cc#L225-L230) asserts that the parent exists and then dereferences it:

```cpp
assert(child->parent());
if (child->parent()->id() == node_update.second.id) {
  continue;
}
```

The assertion is absent from the release build. The null-parent dereference is confirmed; the earlier cause of the inconsistent semantics tree is not yet determined.

### Code sample

No verified minimal runnable app is available yet. We are explicitly separating the production evidence above from a deterministic reproduction. We have not verified that a generic route/slider example reproduces this particular app's failure.

Related upstream work:
- #175041: the same `CreateRemoveReparentedNodesUpdate` / `AXNode::id` crash site.
- #190903: proposed null-parent guard; still open and unmerged when checked on 2026-10-23. We have not tested that custom engine. Its discussion also distinguishes preventing the release crash from fixing malformed semantics updates and keeping the accessibility tree valid.

### Logs

Binary identity was checked against the shipped app, not inferred solely from its version string:

```text
Flutter: 3.47.6
Engine revision: 692136cb6582dbfc5af3fb33c2515a069f2f66d0
Target: windows-x64, release
Affected OS: Windows 11, 10.0.26200.9457
App version: 1.2.5+1

flutter_windows.dll SHA-256:
53238c00bed3fb6e0d822eb18f18dcac093bb30d4502dbfe78b9057690b18699

PE/PDB Debug ID:
17af662f-b466-4079-8c5d-e4ad6cd4d220-1
PDB GUID: 17AF662F-B466-4079-8C5D-E4AD6CD4D220
PDB age: 1
```

The DLL from the official `windows-x64-release` engine archive is byte-identical to the shipped engine DLL. The PDB matches the event module's Debug ID. The symbolization above was obtained with:

```sh
llvm-symbolizer --obj=flutter_windows.dll --relative-address --inlines 0x3c1ca
```

The original crash report also displayed `RtlpInsertUCRBlock` / `RtlpCreateUCREntry` frames obtained by stack scanning. Those scanned frames initially obscured the fault; the actual context instruction pointer is in `flutter_windows.dll` at the location above.

### Flutter Doctor output

A `flutter doctor -v` capture from the affected end-user machine is unavailable. The verified SDK/engine and OS identities are listed above; the engine revision is also the value pinned by [Flutter 3.47.6's engine.version](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/3.47.6/bin/internal/engine.version). We are not presenting another machine's doctor output as the affected environment, and have not yet reproduced this event on a newer SDK.

Could the Windows/accessibility team confirm whether #190903 is intended to cover this signature and which upstream change should restore tree consistency as well as prevent the crash? If this is fully covered by #175041, this report can be consolidated there.

title: [flutter_svg] SvgNetworkLoader parses non-2xx error pages as SVG, hiding the real failure
body:
### What package does this bug report belong to?

flutter_svg

### What target platforms are you seeing this bug on?

Android, iOS

### Have you already upgraded your packages?

Yes

### Dependency versions

flutter_svg 2.3.1 (also present on current `main` of flutter/packages). No other dependencies are involved — the bug is in `SvgNetworkLoader` itself.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Point `SvgPicture.network` (or `SvgNetworkLoader`) at a URL whose server answers with a non-2xx status and an HTML body, e.g. a 404 or a 503 error page.
2. Let the picture load.

### Expected results

The load fails with an error that names the HTTP status and URL, so the cause is visible (e.g. an `http.ClientException`).

### Actual results

`SvgNetworkLoader.prepareMessage` returns `response.bodyBytes` without checking `response.statusCode`, so the HTML error page is handed to the SVG parser and fails as `StateError: Bad state: Invalid SVG data`. The actual 404/503 is lost.

We ran into this in production: during a short backend 503 outage, a request got the server's error page, and our crash reporter showed only "Invalid SVG data".

```dart
// Any URL that returns 404 with an HTML body.
final bytes = await const SvgNetworkLoader('https://example.com/missing.svg')
    .prepareMessage(null);

// StateError: Bad state: Invalid SVG data
```

title: [vector_graphics] SVG <text> is not drawn when the ambient Directionality is RTL
body:
### What package does this bug report belong to?

vector_graphics

### What target platforms are you seeing this bug on?

Android, iOS, macOS

### Have you already upgraded your packages?

Yes

### Dependency versions

<details><summary>pubspec.lock (relevant entries)</summary>

```lock
flutter_svg: 2.3.0
vector_graphics: 1.2.4
vector_graphics_codec: 1.1.13
vector_graphics_compiler: 1.3.2
```

Also reproduced on `flutter/packages` main at b7ec2d0 (vector_graphics 1.2.4).

</details>


### Steps to reproduce

1. Render any SVG that contains `<text>` with `SvgPicture.string` (or `VectorGraphic`) inside `Directionality(textDirection: TextDirection.rtl)`. Any app whose locale is Arabic, Hebrew, Persian or Urdu does this automatically.
2. Compare it with the same SVG under LTR (code sample below).

### Expected results

The text renders at its `x`/`y` in both directions, as it does in browsers. An SVG's text position comes from its own coordinates and `text-anchor`, not from the host app's layout direction.

### Actual results

Under RTL, no `<text>` is drawn at all. Shapes still render. We found this through support reports from Arabic-speaking users where important texts were missing from illustrations.

**Cause:** `FlutterVectorGraphicsListener.onDrawText` (`packages/vector_graphics/lib/src/listener.dart`) builds each paragraph with `ParagraphStyle(textDirection: _textDirection)`, which is the ambient direction, and lays it out with `ParagraphConstraints(width: double.infinity)`. The default `TextAlign.start` resolves to *right* under RTL, so the line sits at the right edge of an infinitely wide box, at x = +∞. `drawParagraph` is then given the correct `Offset`, but the glyphs are infinitely far to the right of it.

The listener already does the horizontal positioning itself (`x`, `dx`, and `text-anchor` through `maxIntrinsicWidth`). The paragraph's own alignment should therefore be neutral, i.e. `TextAlign.left`, whatever the direction.

**Workaround:** wrap the SVG in `Directionality(textDirection: TextDirection.ltr)`.

**Possible follow-up (not verified):** the ambient direction also sets the paragraph's bidi base direction. SVG says the base direction comes from the `direction` property, which defaults to `ltr`. So mixed strings such as `Weight: 2612` may reorder their neutral characters under an RTL app even after this fix. I'm happy to file that separately if maintainers agree it's in scope.

[web] Semantics text fields render autocomplete="off" until focused, ignoring autofillHints
body:
### Steps to reproduce

1. On Flutter Web with semantics enabled, render:

   ```dart
   TextField(
     autofillHints: const <String>[AutofillHints.password],
     obscureText: true,
     decoration: const InputDecoration(labelText: 'Password'),
   )
   ```

   and the same field with `enabled: false`. The `a11y_assessments` test app in flutter/packages has both on `#/text-field-password` since flutter/packages#13243.
2. Inspect the `<input>` elements in the semantics tree without focusing them.
3. Focus the enabled field and inspect again.

### Expected results

Each `<input>` declares its purpose through `autocomplete`, for example `autocomplete="current-password"`, whether or not it has been focused. WCAG 1.3.5 requires the purpose of fields that collect personal data to be programmatically determinable, and automated checkers read the attribute without focusing the field.

### Actual results

| State | `autocomplete` |
|---|---|
| Enabled, never focused | `off` |
| Enabled, focused | `current-password` |
| Disabled | `off` |

The enabled field only switches to `current-password` after it is focused. The disabled field never changes.

### Cause

In `engine/src/flutter/lib/web_ui/lib/src/engine/semantics/text_field.dart`, the semantics `<input>` is created with `autocomplete="off"`. `_updateInputType` only ever sets `autocomplete` for `SemanticsInputType.email`, and it never sets it for obscured fields. Autofill hints are not part of the semantics tree; the engine only learns them from the `TextInput.setClient` configuration, which is sent when the field gains focus, in `text_editing.dart` `AutofillInfo.applyToDomElement`.

For comparison, `keyboardType: TextInputType.emailAddress` does reach the semantics `<input>` before focus, because it travels as `SemanticsInputType.email`.

### Possible fixes

1. Carry autofill hints through semantics, alongside `SemanticsInputType`, and have the web engine apply them to the semantics `<input>` on every update. This is a `dart:ui` and framework API change, following the same path `SemanticsInputType` took.
2. Engine-only stopgap: stop forcing `autocomplete="off"` on obscured fields before focus, either by leaving the attribute unset or by defaulting to `current-password`. Cheaper, but the second option can be wrong for sign-up forms until focus applies the real hint.

### Code sample

<details open><summary>Code sample</summary>

```dart
import 'package:flutter/material.dart';

void main() => runApp(const MaterialApp(home: Demo()));

class Demo extends StatelessWidget {
  const Demo({super.key});

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    return Scaffold(
      body: ListView(
        children: const <Widget>[
          TextField(
            autofillHints: <String>[AutofillHints.password],
            decoration: InputDecoration(labelText: 'Password'),
            obscureText: true,
          ),
          TextField(
            autofillHints: <String>[AutofillHints.password],
            decoration: InputDecoration(labelText: 'Password'),
            enabled: false,
            obscureText: true,
          ),
        ],
      ),
    );
  }
}
```

Enable semantics and run
`[...document.querySelectorAll('[data-semantics-role="text-field"]')].map((e) => e.getAttribute('autocomplete'))`
before and after focusing the first field.

</details>

title: [web][a11y] A Slider enabled after its first frame has no aria-valuetext (its input reads "50") until its value changes
[macOS] System font caches are not refreshed after CoreText registration changes
body:
### Summary

The macOS embedder does not observe `kCTFontManagerRegisteredFontsChangedNotification`. When CoreText changes the registered fonts while an engine remains alive, its cached system font manager/paragraph collection is not refreshed and the framework is not sent `fontsChange`.

`FlutterEngineReloadSystemFonts` already provides both operations, but there is no CoreText notification subscription in macOS `FlutterEngine.mm` on main (`56aa96cf`).

### Reproduction and expected behavior

A focused embedder regression can intercept `engine.embedderAPI.ReloadSystemFonts`, start the engine, then post:

```objc
[[NSNotificationCenter defaultCenter]
    postNotificationName:(__bridge NSString*)kCTFontManagerRegisteredFontsChangedNotification
                  object:nil];
```

Expected: reload the running engine's system fonts on the platform/main thread. Before startup and after shutdown, ignore the notification. A notification delivered on a background thread must be marshalled to the platform thread without retaining an engine that is shutting down.

The current notification setup has no handler for this event. A process-scoped CoreText probe on macOS 27 confirmed that registering and unregistering a test font each emit this notification through `NSNotificationCenter`; no system-wide font installation was needed.

### User-visible observation

This was found while investigating incorrect Chinese glyphs in a long-running FlClash 0.9.1 process (Flutter 3.47.6, macOS 27.0, Apple Silicon). Accessibility strings were correct. The process still mapped a purged PingFang font asset, while a fresh CoreText query resolved PingFang to the reserved UI font collection. Selecting an installed static Chinese font restored the displayed text.

The exact original asset-purge sequence has not been reproduced; the missing notification handling is the scoped defect reported here. An earlier application report may be related: https://github.com/chen08209/FlClash/issues/1948.

### Validation limits

A standalone Objective-C++/GoogleTest harness using the proposed handler and regression test bodies fails 2 of 3 tests without the handler and passes all 3 with it. This is not a run of the full `flutter_desktop_darwin_unittests` target; a complete engine build is still needed.

title: [3.50] Possible cherry-pick: Skia fix for soft hyphens drawn where the line does not break
body: I am not sure whether this qualifies for a cherry-pick, so I am raising it for the release team to decide. Flutter 3.50 is the first release that draws soft hyphens (U+00AD) by default (#185152). Its Skia revision, 0e5d8d1be81b, does not include https://skia-review.googlesource.com/c/skia/+/1378356 (ee9f718ac9). From my testing, 3.50 therefore also draws a hyphen where the line does not break at the soft hyphen: at the end of the text, or before a space or a line break. The fix has been on master since #194331 (Oct 14). As far as I can tell, applying it would need a Skia branch for 3.50 at 0e5d8d1be81b with ee9f718ac9 cherry-picked; in a local test it applied cleanly. **Impacted Users:** Apps on Flutter 3.50 on native platforms that display text with a soft hyphen at the end of the text or right before a space or line break. **Impact Description:** A stray hyphen appears in the rendered text, for example "Thanks for your cooperation-" for text that ends in a soft hyphen. **Workaround:** `hyphens: Hyphens.hidden` on `Text`, `RichText` or `TextPainter` turns off hyphen rendering. Widgets built on `EditableText`, such as `TextField` and `SelectableText`, do not have a `hyphens` parameter, so I do not think they have a workaround. **Risk:** I believe it is low: the fix is a seven-line check in `TextLine::createSoftHyphen`, and it has been on Flutter master since Oct 14. **Test Coverage:** The Skia change added `SkParagraph_SoftHyphenAtEndOfParagraph`, `SoftHyphenBeforeSpace` and `SoftHyphenBeforeHardBreak`. **Validation Steps:** With the FlutterTest font at 10px and `Hyphens.manual`, `'hello wor\u00AD'` at width 1000 has `longestLine` 100 on 3.50 and 90 with the fix. `'abc\u00AD def'` at width 45 gives 40 and 30. `'abc\u00AD\ndef'` at width 1000 gives 40 and 30.

title: [macOS] Clipboard.hasStrings synchronously reads pasteboard text on the main thread, causing AppHang
body:
### Summary

On macOS, the engine implements `Clipboard.hasStrings` by synchronously retrieving pasteboard text on the platform/main thread. We observed production AppHang reports with that thread waiting in `NSPasteboard stringForType:` / `CFPasteboardRequestDataFromDaemon` while servicing this availability query.

This report concerns the **macOS engine implementation of the availability query**, separately from the framework deciding when to issue it.

Related:
- #190654: proactive `EditableText` clipboard queries.
- #190707: limits clipboard checks to focused/editable fields.
- [Our original macOS evidence and tested standalone widget probe](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/issues/190654#issuecomment-6381957137).
- [Fury76's follow-up recommending a separate engine issue](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/issues/190654#issuecomment-6382604114).

### Observed behavior and environment

We observed **2 AppHang reports affecting 1 user**, in a production macOS app (app release 1.2.5+31), on **macOS 26.5.1 / MacBookAir10,1 (Apple Silicon)**. The reports indicate a main-thread hang of at least 2000ms, not a crash.

In a representative event with navigation breadcrumbs:
1. The user entered a sentence editor.
2. An unnamed editing dialog was pushed.
3. An AppHang was recorded approximately 2 seconds later, with the main-thread stack below.

The route breadcrumb does not identify which individual dialog/field caused the production query. We do not know the clipboard producer or its contents, and cannot yet deterministically reproduce the real daemon stall. No user/account identifiers, clipboard contents or learning content are included in this report.

### Main-thread stack

Shown from caller to sampled blocking frame:

```text
FlutterRunLoop.performExpiredTasks                       FlutterRunLoop.swift:148
-[FlutterEngine postMainThreadTask:targetTimeInNanoseconds:] block
                                                        FlutterEngine.mm:1841
FlutterEngineRunTask
flutter::EmbedderEngine::RunTask
flutter::EmbedderTaskRunner::PostTask
flutter::PlatformViewEmbedder::HandlePlatformMessage      platform_view_embedder.cc:138
-[FlutterEngine engineCallbackOnPlatformMessage:]        FlutterEngine.mm:1320
-[FlutterMethodChannel setMethodCallHandler:] block      FlutterChannels.mm:315
-[FlutterEngine addInternalPlugins] block                FlutterEngine.mm:1444
-[FlutterEngine handleMethodCall:result:]                 FlutterEngine.mm:1590
-[FlutterEngine clipboardHasStrings]                     FlutterEngine.mm:1635
-[FlutterPasteboard stringForType:]                      FlutterEngine.mm:296
-[NSPasteboard stringForType:]
-[NSPasteboard _dataForType:index:usesPboardTypes:combinesItems:securityScoped:]
-[NSPasteboard _dataWithoutConversionForTypeIdentifier:securityScoped:]
CFPasteboardCopyData
___onqueue_CFPasteboardRequestDataFromDaemon_block_invoke
CFRunLoop / mach_msg / mach_msg2_trap
```

This establishes that the availability query entered synchronous pasteboard content retrieval. It does not establish why the pasteboard daemon/provider was slow, or that every query stalls.

### Engine source evidence (Flutter 3.47.8)

The same implementation is present in the released **3.47.8** source:

1. [Platform method dispatch](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/3.47.8/engine/src/flutter/shell/platform/darwin/macos/framework/Source/FlutterEngine.mm#L1589-L1590):

```objc
} else if ([call.method isEqualToString:@"Clipboard.hasStrings"]) {
  result(@{@"value" : @([self clipboardHasStrings])});
```

2. [Availability check fetches the string](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/3.47.8/engine/src/flutter/shell/platform/darwin/macos/framework/Source/FlutterEngine.mm#L1634-L1636):

```objc
- (BOOL)clipboardHasStrings {
  return [self.pasteboard stringForType:NSPasteboardTypeString].length > 0;
}
```

3. [Pasteboard wrapper delegates to NSPasteboard](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/3.47.8/engine/src/flutter/shell/platform/darwin/macos/framework/Source/FlutterEngine.mm#L295-L297):

```objc
- (NSString*)stringForType:(NSPasteboardType)dataType {
  return [[NSPasteboard generalPasteboard] stringForType:dataType];
}
```

The source snippets were checked against the installed SDK and the GitHub 3.47.8 tag. This confirms that the engine path remains in 3.47.8; it is not a claim that the affected production app was built with 3.47.8.

### Trigger reproduction and its limits

The standalone widget probe linked above was run on **Flutter 3.47.8 / Dart 3.13.7** with a macOS target-platform variant and a mocked `SystemChannels.platform`. It confirmed:
- An ordinary unfocused TextField issues `Clipboard.hasStrings` on initialization and resume.
- Setting `enableInteractiveSelection: false` and `contextMenuBuilder: null` does not prevent those queries in that SDK.
- The application's own clipboard helper is not involved; the call originates at `EditableTextState.initState -> ClipboardStatusNotifier.addListener -> update`.
- No Dart `Clipboard.getData` call is needed to reach this native string-read path.

Those tests prove the trigger, **not the native >=2s stall**: they mock the channel and do not read the actual clipboard.

Fury76 subsequently ran the probe against **3.44.2 + #190707** and reported no init/resume queries for unfocused fields, one query when a selectable field gains focus, and no queries for a non-selectable field. We have not independently tested that PR. It reduces unnecessary triggers, but the remaining legitimate `hasStrings` calls can still reach the macOS native implementation described here.

### Expected result

Checking whether text is available to paste should avoid synchronously fetching/coercing the pasteboard text on the main thread merely to determine availability. Normal user-initiated paste and its existing behavior should remain supported.

An engine fix should explicitly consider empty-string and convertible-text cases; this report does not prescribe an untested replacement API. Adding a timeout only around the Dart Future would not release a main thread already blocked in the synchronous native read.

title: [Flutter GPU] Expose texture size limits (max 2D size, array layers, 3D size)
body:
### Use case

Apps that size GPU textures to their data need the device's limits to decide whether something fits and how to split it. Examples: large images and maps split into tiles, texture atlases, terrain, and in my case 3D volumes rendered with Flutter GPU (through flutter_scene). A volume either goes on the GPU as one resource or as a few, or it stays on a slower CPU path.

`GpuContext` exposes feature checks (`doesSupportTextureArrays`, `doesSupportOffscreenMSAA`, …) and `maxSamplerAnisotropy`, but no size limits. So I hard-code 4096 × 4096, a value I expect every target to support. On desktop that wastes most of the device: a 512³ volume needs four 4096² pages where one 8192² page or one array texture would do. I also can't tell a device that supports less from one that supports more.

With 2D arrays (#190036) and 3D textures (#195222), the questions become "how many layers can this array have" and "how deep can this volume be". Today the answer is either a guess or a failed allocation.

Impeller already has a similar value internally, `Capabilities::GetMaximumRenderPassAttachmentSize()`, but it isn't exposed in Dart and only covers render targets.

### Proposal

Read-only getters on `GpuContext`, filled from the backend:

```dart
gpu.gpuContext.maxTextureSize2D;      // largest width/height of a 2D texture
gpu.gpuContext.maxTextureArrayLayers; // for texture2DArray
gpu.gpuContext.maxTextureSize3D;      // once 3D textures exist
gpu.gpuContext.maxRenderTargetSize;   // GetMaximumRenderPassAttachmentSize
```

Sources per backend:

- **Vulkan:** `VkPhysicalDeviceLimits.maxImageDimension2D`, `maxImageArrayLayers`, `maxImageDimension3D`.
- **OpenGL ES:** `GL_MAX_TEXTURE_SIZE`, `GL_MAX_ARRAY_TEXTURE_LAYERS`, `GL_MAX_3D_TEXTURE_SIZE`.
- **Metal:** there is no runtime query, but the values are fixed per GPU family in Apple's feature set tables, and Impeller already checks GPU families. They do differ: the largest 2D texture is 16,384 on Apple3 through Apple9 and on Mac2, but 32,768 on Apple10. A hard-coded value is either too low for new devices or too high for old ones.

Optional and less important: a hint for how much texture memory the app can reasonably use (Metal has `recommendedMaxWorkingSetSize`; Vulkan has memory heap sizes and the memory budget extension). I set my own budget today, and a device value would help pick it, but the size limits matter more.

Related: #190036 (2D arrays), #195222 (3D textures), #195223 (16-bit formats), and #193868 (compute device limits, the same idea for compute).

title: [Flutter GPU] Single-channel 16-bit texture formats (r16UNorm, r16SNorm, r16Float)
body:
### Use case

A lot of real-world data is one channel at 16 bits:

- depth camera images (LiDAR and structured-light sensors usually deliver depth as 16-bit millimetres)
- terrain elevation (DEM tiles are commonly 16-bit)
- scientific scalar fields and simulation output
- single-channel masks that need more than 8 bits

I'm rendering this kind of data with Flutter GPU (through flutter_scene), including 3D volumes; the 3D textures request is #195222. `PixelFormat` has no single-channel 16-bit format, so the options today are:

| Format | Bytes per value | Hardware filtering | Problem |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `r32Float` | 4 | Optional on GLES/WebGL2 and Vulkan | Twice the memory; a 512³ volume is 512 MB instead of 256 MB |
| `r16g16b16a16Float` | 8 | Yes | Four times the memory for one channel |
| `r8g8UNormInt`, value split into two bytes | 2 | No: filtering the bytes separately gives wrong values | Manual filtering in the shader |
| `r8g8b8a8UNormInt`, two values per texel (what I ship) | 2 | No | Manual filtering and extra addressing |

I pack two 16-bit values per RGBA8 texel. That keeps memory at 2 bytes per value, but every trilinear sample becomes 8 fetches with byte decoding plus 7 `mix` calls in the shader. A single-channel 16-bit format would give the same memory cost with one hardware-filtered fetch.

Precision is why a normalized format matters, not just `r16Float`. A normalized 16-bit format stores 65,536 evenly spaced levels, which is exactly what 16-bit source data has. `r16Float` has an 11-bit significand, so integers above 2048 can't all be represented. For depth in millimetres, anything beyond about 2 m loses single-millimetre steps, and beyond 4 m the step is 4 mm.

### Proposal

Add to `PixelFormat` (Impeller and Flutter GPU):

- `r16UNormInt`
- `r16SNormInt`
- `r16Float`

And a way to ask what a format supports on the current device, since normalized 16-bit is optional on some backends:

```dart
gpu.gpuContext.doesSupportFormat(gpu.PixelFormat.r16UNormInt);   // sample at all
gpu.gpuContext.isFormatFilterable(gpu.PixelFormat.r16UNormInt);  // linear filtering
```

Backend support, as far as I can tell:

- **Metal:** `R16Unorm`, `R16Snorm` and `R16Float` are available and filterable on all GPU families.
- **Vulkan:** `R16_SFLOAT` sampling and linear filtering are mandatory. `R16_UNORM` and `R16_SNORM` are optional, so they need `vkGetPhysicalDeviceFormatProperties`.
- **OpenGL ES 3.0:** `R16F` is filterable in core. `R16`/`R16_SNORM` need `EXT_texture_norm16`, which also exists for WebGL2 (community approved).

So `r16Float` could be available everywhere, and the normalized formats where the device reports them. Apps would prefer `r16UNormInt` and fall back to `r16Float` or packing.

The same query would also answer a question apps can't ask today: whether `r32Float` can be filtered linearly. That is optional on GLES (`OES_texture_float_linear`) and Vulkan.

`r16g16` variants would round this out (for example vector fields and normal maps), but single-channel matters most to me.

Related: #195222 (3D textures), #195224 (texture size limits), and #186309 (vertex formats gated by backend capability, a similar pattern).

title: [Flutter GPU] 3D textures (texture3D / sampler3D)
body:
### Use case

I'm building a volume renderer on Flutter GPU (through flutter_scene) for 3D scalar data: simulation output such as fluid density or temperature fields, voxel scans, and signed distance fields. It draws arbitrary slice planes, maximum intensity projections and direct volume rendering, all ray-marched in a fragment shader over a volume that stays resident on the GPU.

A volume is a 3D grid of values, and the natural resource for it is a 3D texture: one bind, hardware trilinear filtering, and clamping on all three axes. Flutter GPU has `texture2D`, `textureCube` and, since #190036, `texture2DArray`, but no 3D texture.

What I do today instead:

- Slices are laid out as tiles on up to four 2D atlas pages of at most 4096 × 4096 RGBA8 texels. Each texel packs two 16-bit values (red/green and blue/alpha, high byte first).
- Every voxel read computes a page, a tile row and column, and a texel inside the tile. It then picks one of four bound samplers with branches and decodes two bytes.
- Hardware filtering can't be used on packed bytes, so one trilinear sample is 8 of those reads plus 7 `mix` calls in the shader. During interaction the renderer falls back to nearest sampling and only draws a trilinear frame once the view is still.
- Capacity is capped by the page layout at about 128 M voxels (512² × 512), and every page costs a sampler slot.

2D arrays (#188776) remove the tile arithmetic between slices, but filtering along the slice axis still needs two fetches and a manual `mix`. A 3D texture would make the shader's fetch a single `texture()` call.

3D textures also show up well beyond volume rendering: 3D look-up tables for colour grading, noise volumes for clouds and fog, smoke and fire simulations, voxel global illumination, and light probe volumes. This can't be done in a package, because the engine has to create and bind the resource.

All of Flutter GPU's backends support 3D textures natively: Metal (`MTLTextureType3D`), Vulkan (`VK_IMAGE_TYPE_3D`) and OpenGL ES 3.0 (`GL_TEXTURE_3D`, `glTexImage3D`). WebGL2 has them too, which matters if Flutter GPU reaches the web.

### Proposal

Following the shape of the 2D array work:

```dart
final volume = gpu.gpuContext.createTexture(
  gpu.StorageMode.hostVisible,
  width,
  height,
  depth: depth,                         // new; must be 1 unless texture3D
  textureType: gpu.TextureType.texture3D,
  format: gpu.PixelFormat.r8g8UNormInt, // or a 16-bit format, see #195223
);

// Whole volume, or one z-slice at a time so large volumes can stream in as
// they are produced (the same meaning `slice` already has for arrays).
volume.overwrite(sliceBytes, slice: z);

final sampler = gpu.SamplerOptions(
  minFilter: gpu.MinMagFilter.linear,
  magFilter: gpu.MinMagFilter.linear,
  widthAddressMode: gpu.SamplerAddressMode.clampToEdge,
  heightAddressMode: gpu.SamplerAddressMode.clampToEdge,
  depthAddressMode: gpu.SamplerAddressMode.clampToEdge, // new
);
```

```glsl
uniform sampler3D volume;
float v = texture(volume, uvw).r;
```

Scope as I understand it:

- Impeller: `TextureType::kTexture3D` with a depth extent in `TextureDescriptor`, mapped to the backend type on Metal, Vulkan and GLES. Uploads per z-slice. An address mode for the third axis (Metal `rAddressMode`, Vulkan `addressModeW`, GL `TEXTURE_WRAP_R`).
- impellerc and shader bundles: reflect `sampler3D` (I haven't checked whether this already works).
- Flutter GPU: `TextureType.texture3D`, a `depth` parameter, `depthAddressMode`, and a capability check like `doesSupportTextureArrays`. On GLES this probably has the same limit as arrays, since a shader bundle carries one GLES variant and `sampler3D` needs GLSL ES 3.0.
- A device limit for the maximum 3D size, so apps can plan volume sizes (see #195224).

Rendering into a 3D texture or writing to it from compute would be nice later, but sampling and uploading alone would let me drop the atlas.

Related: #188776 / #190036 (2D arrays), #188474 (compute), #195223 (16-bit formats) and #195224 (texture size limits).

body:
### Steps to reproduce
1. Use in_app_purchase_storekit 0.4.13+1 to 0.4.15 with StoreKit 2 (the default).
2. Have Transaction.currentEntitlements yield at least one `.unverified` result.
3. Call `InAppPurchase.instance.restorePurchases()`.

### Expected results
The Dart future fails with a PlatformException `storekit2_restore_failed`, as the Swift code intends.

### Actual results
The app terminates with an uncaught NSInternalInconsistencyException "Unsupported value for standard codec".

`InAppPurchasePlugin+StoreKit2.swift` (`restorePurchases`) builds `unverifiedPurchases` as `[UInt64: (receipt: String, error: Error?)]` and passes it as the `details` of `PigeonError(code: "storekit2_restore_failed", ...)`. `wrapError` in `StoreKit2Messages.g.swift` hands `details` to the standard codec unchanged. A Swift tuple bridges to `__SwiftValue`, which `FlutterStandardCodec.mm` (`FlutterStandardCodecObjcTypeUnknown`) meets with `NSCAssert(NO, @"Unsupported value for standard codec")`. The assertion is present in the ios-release Flutter.framework (Flutter 3.47.1), so release builds crash too. Reproduced by encoding the same payload with the release codec (exit 134).

### Suggested fix
Pass encodable details, for example the transaction ids as strings (`unverifiedPurchases.keys.map { String($0) }`), or a list of maps holding only strings.

### Flutter version
3.47.1

body:
CVE-2026-111497 is an out-of-bounds write in the Google Brotli decoder, already public. It affects 1.0.3 through 1.2.0 and is fixed in 1.0.10, 1.1.1, and 1.2.1.

`master` and `stable` still pin `engine/src/flutter/third_party/brotli` to `350100a5bb9d9671aca85213b2ec7a70a361b0cd`, which is Brotli 1.1.0. Checked on 24 Oct 2026, including Flutter 3.47.6 and 3.47.7. `c/dec/decode.c` at that commit does not have the fix.

That decoder is linked into the web runtime (`canvaskit.wasm`, `skwasm.wasm`, `skwasm_heavy.wasm`), where it decodes WOFF2 fonts. It is not linked into the iOS or Android engine binaries.

title: [iOS] Flutter UI thread (io.flutter.1) exits while process stays alive — permanent black screen, only force-quit recovers (Impeller)
body:
### Summary

On a physical iPhone (iOS 26.x, standard Flutter app, no add-to-app), the Flutter **UI thread (`io.flutter.1`) exits while the process stays alive**. The app renders a permanent black screen, stops responding, and all Dart-side logging stops abruptly. Only force-quitting and relaunching recovers. Happens on Impeller (default); with `FLTEnableImpeller=NO` (Skia) the same sequence has not reproduced so far.

### Environment

- Flutter 3.41.4 (stable), engine revision e4b8dca3f1
- iOS 26.x physical device (iPhone, arm64); standard app template (AppDelegate/FlutterAppDelegate, single engine, no UIScene migration)
- Impeller enabled (default); no `FLTEnableImpeller` key before the A/B test
- file_picker 10.3.10 (system `UIDocumentPickerViewController`)
- Reproduced twice in one morning under Xcode Run (debugger attached), plus 8 occurrences across 22 days on TestFlight builds

### Steps to reproduce (best-known sequence)

1. Log in (SMS code input — keyboard shown/hidden).
2. Let BLE auto-sync churn for a while (many platform-channel events).
3. Import files via the system document picker 4 times in a row: 3 duplicates (progress sheet ends in a "duplicate" failed state, dismissed via button) + 1 new file (sheet auto-closes 1.2s after done).
4. A few seconds to ~3 minutes later the screen goes black.

### Evidence captured while the screen was black (debugger attached)

`thread list` (lldb) — the UI thread is **gone**; every other thread is present and parked in normal idle waits:

```
* thread #1: main thread — mach_msg2_trap (runloop, healthy)
  thread #17: 'io.flutter.1.raster' — mach_msg2_trap (fml message loop, idle)
  thread #18: 'io.flutter.1.io' — mach_msg2_trap (idle)
  thread #19..21: 'io.worker.1..3' — cond_wait (idle)
  thread #22: 'dart:io EventHandler' — kevent
  ... (no thread named 'io.flutter.1' anywhere)
```

- `bt all`: no deadlocks, no locks held, no Metal waits — all remaining threads healthy idle.
- View hierarchy debugger: `UIWindowScene (Foreground Active)` → `UIWindow` → `FlutterViewController` → `FlutterView` intact; `UITextEffectsWindow` still holds the system keyboard; scene content renders pure black.
- Process metrics at black screen: alive, CPU ~8%, memory ~474 MB.
- All app logging (which runs on the UI isolate) stops at the moment of death; platform-side threads keep working (UIKit responsive).
- **No crash report anywhere**: nothing on-device (Settings → Analytics), nothing in Sentry (native integration enabled; SentryANRTracker only watches the main thread, which is healthy), and with the debugger attached there is no exception and no signal — the thread simply ceases to exist.

### Historical signature

8 occurrences over 22 days on TestFlight builds, each with the same fingerprint: all Dart logging stops mid-activity, then the user (seeing a black screen) force-quits and relaunches. Triggers observed both right after repeated document-picker excursions and around BLE platform-channel bursts.

### A/B result so far

- Impeller builds: black screen twice in one morning (same repro sequence), historical 8 deaths.
- `FLTEnableImpeller=NO` (Skia) build: full repro sequence (picker x4, BLE storm, recording, delete, playback) survived with the process and UI thread intact so far.

### What we're asking

1. What code paths can terminate the Flutter UI thread (`io.flutter.1`) without taking down the process — engine shutdown, task-runner teardown, or a swallowed thread-exit?
2. Any diagnostics the team wants from a live reproduction? We can reproduce under the debugger on demand and can capture thread state, engine logs, or add instrumentation.
3. If useful: a watchdog that detects UI-thread death and at least logs/fails loudly (today the failure is completely silent — no crash, no report, nothing).

Related: #183814 — same symptom family (iOS black screen with Impeller), but in that report the engine threads survive and Dart can still schedule frames; in ours the UI thread itself is gone.

title: [Flutter GPU] CommandBuffer.submit completion callback is invoked twice when the Vulkan submit fails, crashing the process (SIGSEGV)
body:
### Steps to reproduce

1. On an Android device using Impeller Vulkan, create a `gpu.CommandBuffer`, encode any render pass, and call `submit(completionCallback: (ok) { ... })`.
2. Have the Vulkan queue submission fail. We hit it after `VK_ERROR_DEVICE_LOST` (Adreno, Galaxy Z Fold6); any failure of `CommandQueueVK::Submit` takes the same path.

There is no deterministic way to make a Vulkan submit fail from Dart. The defect is visible by reading the two functions below, and the crash backtrace matches it.

### Expected results

`completionCallback` is called once with `false`, and `submit` throws `Failed to submit CommandBuffer`.

### Actual results

The callback is called with `false` once, and then the process crashes on the UI thread (SIGSEGV, null-pointer read at 0x8).

The completion callback is invoked twice:

- `impeller/renderer/backend/vulkan/command_queue_vk.cc`, `CommandQueueVK::Submit`: an `fml::ScopedCleanupClosure` ("Success or failure, you only get to submit once.") calls `completion_callback(CommandBuffer::Status::kError)` on every early return, including a failed `AddFence`/queue submit.
- `lib/gpu/command_buffer.cc`, `CommandBuffer::Submit`: after `context_->GetCommandQueue()->Submit(...)` returns a non-ok status, it calls `combined_completion_callback(impeller::CommandBuffer::Status::kError)` again. On master this is the Vulkan/Metal branch (around line 228); the GLES branch has the same pattern (around line 219).

The Dart-facing callback built in `InternalFlutterGpu_CommandBuffer_Submit` is a `fml::MakeCopyable` lambda that moves its `std::unique_ptr<tonic::DartPersistentValue>` into the posted UI task. The first invocation moves it out. The second invocation posts a task holding a null pointer, and that task dereferences it at `callback->dart_state().lock()` (`lib/gpu/command_buffer.cc:237` in 3.47.7).

Possible fix: drop the second invocation in `flutter::gpu::CommandBuffer::Submit` when the queue already reports the failure, or make the callback idempotent.

Workaround: call `submit()` without a `completionCallback`. The failure then only surfaces as the thrown exception, and the process survives.

### Code sample

```dart
final cb = gpu.gpuContext.createCommandBuffer();
cb.createRenderPass(gpu.RenderTarget.singleColor(gpu.ColorAttachment(texture: tex)));
// ... draws ...
cb.submit(completionCallback: (ok) => debugPrint('gpu $ok'));
// When the Vulkan submit fails: "gpu false" is printed, then SIGSEGV.
```

### Logs

Verbatim. The two `LADDER` lines are our test app's own: the first prints the exception `submit` threw, the second prints the completion callback's `false`.

```
10-24 19:41:13.060 25743 25743 E flutter : [ERROR:flutter/impeller/renderer/backend/vulkan/command_queue_vk.cc(72)] Break on 'ImpellerValidationBreak' to inspect point of failure: Failed to submit command: ErrorDeviceLost
10-24 19:41:13.060 25743 25743 I flutter : LADDER S4 FAILED at frame 5: Exception: Failed to submit CommandBuffer
10-24 19:41:13.061 25743 25743 I flutter : LADDER S4 frame 5 gpu FAILED
10-24 19:41:13.062 25743 25766 E flutter : [ERROR:flutter/impeller/renderer/backend/vulkan/swapchain/khr/khr_swapchain_impl_vk.cc(492)] Break on 'ImpellerValidationBreak' to inspect point of failure: Could not wait on render semaphore: ErrorDeviceLost
10-24 19:41:13.062 25743 25743 F libc    : Fatal signal 11 (SIGSEGV), code 1 (SEGV_MAPERR), fault addr 0x8 in tid 25743 (arine_gpu_spike), pid 25743 (arine_gpu_spike)
```

Symbolized with the published `android-arm64-profile/symbols.zip` for engine `deb287481e3ce9468f3434937ced4240a70539ca` (BuildId e154c644713cf2bfb7a6ebb020fc0907fdaa340e):

```
#00 std::weak_ptr<flutter::PlatformIsolateManager>::lock() const      (shared_ptr.h:1369)
#01 fml::internal::CopyableLambda<InternalFlutterGpu_CommandBuffer_Submit::$_0::operator()(impeller::CommandBuffer::Status)::'lambda'()>::operator()()
                                                                       lib/gpu/command_buffer.cc:237:56
```

title: [Flutter GPU] Vulkan device lost on Adreno when a render pass with depth is sampled by the next render pass in the same command buffer
body:
### Steps to reproduce

On a Galaxy Z Fold6 (SM-F956U1, Android 16, Adreno, Vulkan driver 0762.41, build f6b5df5188, "Using the Impeller rendering backend (Vulkan)"), Flutter 3.47.7 stable, profile build, Flutter GPU enabled:

1. Create three sets of textures, rotated each frame: a colour target, a `defaultDepthStencilFormat` depth texture (`StorageMode.deviceTransient`), and an output texture.
2. Each frame, in **one** `CommandBuffer`:
   - render pass 1: a mesh drawn into the colour target, with the depth attachment (depth write on, compare `less`);
   - render pass 2: a full-screen draw into the output texture that samples pass 1's colour target (`bindTexture`).
3. `submit()`, then display the output with `asImage()`.

```dart
final cb = gpu.gpuContext.createCommandBuffer();
final p1 = cb.createRenderPass(gpu.RenderTarget.singleColor(
  gpu.ColorAttachment(texture: colour[i], clearValue: vm.Vector4(0, 0, 0, 1)),
  depthStencilAttachment: gpu.DepthStencilAttachment(texture: depth[i], depthClearValue: 1.0),
));
p1
  ..bindPipeline(meshPipeline)
  ..setDepthWriteEnable(true)
  ..setDepthCompareOperation(gpu.CompareFunction.less)
  ..setCullMode(gpu.CullMode.backFace);
// bind vertex/index buffers and uniforms, then:
p1.drawIndexed(indexCount);

final p2 = cb.createRenderPass(gpu.RenderTarget.singleColor(gpu.ColorAttachment(texture: out[i])));
p2
  ..bindPipeline(fullscreenPipeline)
  ..bindVertexBuffer(gpu.BufferView(quad, offsetInBytes: 0, lengthInBytes: quad.sizeInBytes))
  ..bindTexture(toneFragment.getUniformSlot('hdr'), colour[i],
      sampler: gpu.SamplerOptions(minFilter: gpu.MinMagFilter.linear, magFilter: gpu.MinMagFilter.linear))
  ..draw(3);
cb.submit();
```

### Expected results

Frames render. The same code renders indefinitely on Impeller OpenGLES (Android emulator).

### Actual results

For frames 0–4, each frame's encode + `submit` blocks the UI thread for about 275 ms, and the completion callbacks of frames 0–2 arrive 570–850 ms after submit. On the same device, the variants that work below take about 1 ms to encode and complete in 2–3 ms. At frame 5, `submit` fails with `ErrorDeviceLost`, and the Adreno driver logs a GPU-fault snapshot (`Adreno-GSL: <log_gpu_snapshot:476>`). Every UI frame after that also fails (`Could not wait on render semaphore: ErrorDeviceLost`), so the app stops drawing.

We ran a set of variants, each in its own process:

| Variant | Result |
|---|---|
| Mesh + depth into rgba8, displayed directly (no second pass) | ok |
| rgba16f target cleared only, never drawn or sampled | ok |
| Mesh into rgba16f, no depth, not sampled | ok |
| Mesh + depth into rgba16f, not sampled | ok |
| rgba16f cleared (no draw), then sampled linear / nearest in the same command buffer | ok |
| **Mesh + depth, then sampled in the same command buffer, rgba8 colour** | **device lost at frame 5** |
| **Same, rgba16f colour** | **device lost at frame 5** |
| **Same, at 256 × 256** | **device lost at frame 5** |
| **Same, with 4x MSAA resolved into the sampled texture** | **device lost at frame 5** |
| Same two passes split across **two** command buffers | ok (360 frames) |

So it is not the format, size or MSAA. It is a drawn pass with a depth attachment followed, in the same command buffer, by a pass sampling its colour attachment.

The Khronos validation layer (1.4.363, packaged in the APK) was requested with `--enable-vulkan-validation` on two variants, and printed no messages. The loader found the layer. But Impeller's "Vulkan validations are enabled." confirmation is INFO-level and is not printed in a profile build, so we cannot confirm validation was actually active.

If a completion callback is passed to `submit`, the process then crashes with SIGSEGV (#195247). Without a callback the process survives, but Impeller's device is lost and the UI does not recover.

Possibly related: #192539 (the Vulkan framebuffer cache is keyed only on part of the attachment set). Our variants used each colour texture with a single attachment set, so the cache should not have been involved.

### Logs

```
I flutter : [IMPORTANT:flutter/shell/platform/android/android_context_vk_impeller.cc(62)] Using the Impeller rendering backend (Vulkan).
W Adreno-GSL: <log_gpu_snapshot:476>: panel.gpuSnapshotPath is not set.not generating user snapshot
E flutter : [ERROR:flutter/impeller/renderer/backend/vulkan/command_queue_vk.cc(72)] Break on 'ImpellerValidationBreak' to inspect point of failure: Failed to submit command: ErrorDeviceLost
E flutter : [ERROR:flutter/impeller/renderer/backend/vulkan/swapchain/khr/khr_swapchain_impl_vk.cc(492)] Break on 'ImpellerValidationBreak' to inspect point of failure: Could not wait on render semaphore: ErrorDeviceLost
```

title: [ios] Apple Pencil hover is reported as PointerDeviceKind.mouse; hover zOffset is never forwarded
body:
### Steps to reproduce

1. iPad that supports Apple Pencil hover (M2 iPad Pro or later, iPad mini A17 Pro), iPadOS 16.1+, with Pencil Hover enabled in Settings > Apple Pencil.
2. Run the code sample below (or any app that reads `PointerEvent.kind` from a global pointer route, or uses `MouseRegion.onHover`).
3. Hover the Pencil over the screen without touching it, then tap.

### Expected results

Hover events from the Pencil carry `PointerDeviceKind.stylus`, or at least a non-zero `PointerData.distance` taken from `UIHoverGestureRecognizer.zOffset`, so an app can tell a hovering Pencil from a mouse or trackpad cursor. The tap that follows is `PointerDeviceKind.stylus`, so hover and touch from the same device agree.

### Actual results

Hover events carry `PointerDeviceKind.mouse` and `distance` is 0. In `FlutterViewController.mm`, `hoverEvent:` sets `pointer_data.kind = kMouse` unconditionally and uses the hover recognizer's address as the device id, so a Pencil hover is indistinguishable from a Magic Trackpad cursor. The Pencil's touch then arrives as `kStylus` via `DeviceKindFromTouchType`. Android fills `PointerData.distance` for stylus hover height; iOS never does, even though `zOffset` is available on the recognizer.

Consequence: an app that chooses touch vs cursor layout from `kind` (hover affordances, drag vs long-press-drag) flips to cursor mode as the Pencil approaches and back to touch mode on the tap, rebuilding the tapped widget mid-gesture and losing the tap. Users have reported this since Dec 2024; it works with Pencil Hover disabled.

Source at 3.47.2: https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/3.47.2/engine/src/flutter/shell/platform/darwin/ios/framework/Source/FlutterViewController.mm (`hoverEvent:` and `DeviceKindFromTouchType`).

Related: #162462 covers `DeviceKindFromTouchType` conflating direct and indirect touch; this is the hover side of the same mapping.

```dart
import 'package:flutter/gestures.dart';
import 'package:flutter/material.dart';

void main() {
  runApp(const MaterialApp(home: Scaffold(body: Center(child: Text('Hover, then tap')))));

    if (e is PointerHoverEvent || e is PointerDownEvent) {
```

title: [Impeller][Android][Vulkan] SIGABRT in Mali driver when GC finalizes a ui.Image after the Activity is destroyed (TextureVK::~TextureVK)
body:
### Steps to reproduce

We can't reproduce this on demand. It comes from production crash reports (~20 events in 7 weeks, release builds only). The common pattern in the breadcrumbs:

1. Release build on an Android device with an ARM Mali GPU, using Impeller's default Vulkan backend.
2. The app holds `ui.Image`s, including `Image.clone()`d handles. In our case, a session-replay SDK (Microsoft Clarity, `clarity_flutter` 1.7.1) clones painted images and later reads them back with `toByteData` / `Picture.toImage`.
3. The user leaves the app. Breadcrumbs show `MainActivity` going through `paused → stopped → destroyed`, and then the app goes to the background.
4. An old-space GC runs on a Dart worker thread, finalizes a `CanvasImage`, and the resulting `TextureVK` destruction aborts inside `libGLES_mali.so`.

### Expected results

Releasing an image texture after the Activity/surface is gone should not abort the process.

### Actual results

The process crashes with `SIGABRT` from the Mali driver.

### Stack trace (symbolicated against engine `035316565ad77281a75305515e4682e6c4c6f7ca`, android-arm64-release)

Innermost frame first:

```
#00 libc.so                abort
#01 libc.so
#02 libGLES_mali.so
#03 libGLES_mali.so
#04 libflutter.so +0x7e7a54  impeller::FramebufferAndRenderPass::~FramebufferAndRenderPass()   impeller/renderer/backend/vulkan/texture_source_vk.h:20
#05 libflutter.so +0x7ed954  impeller::TextureSourceVK::~TextureSourceVK()                    impeller/renderer/backend/vulkan/texture_source_vk.cc:11
#06 libflutter.so +0x7edb0c  impeller::TextureVK::~TextureVK()                                 impeller/renderer/backend/vulkan/texture_vk.cc:25
#07 libflutter.so +0x470c40  std::__shared_weak_count::__release_shared()
#08 libflutter.so +0xa13a68  (outlined)
#09 libflutter.so +0x7942b4  impeller::DlImageImpeller::~DlImageImpeller()                     impeller/display_list/dl_image_impeller.cc:77
#10 libflutter.so +0x827844  flutter::CanvasImage::~CanvasImage()                              lib/ui/painting/image.cc:31
#11 libflutter.so +0x81731c  fml::RefCountedThreadSafe<flutter::CanvasImage>::Release()
#12 libflutter.so +0x94c344  dart::MarkingWeakVisitor::VisitHandle(unsigned long)              runtime/vm/dart_api_impl.cc:728
#13 libflutter.so +0x94eff0  dart::ParallelMarkTask::RunEnteredIsolateGroup()
#14 libflutter.so +0x956d74  dart::SafepointHandler::RunTasks(...)
#15 libflutter.so +0x95275c  dart::PageSpace::CollectGarbage(...)
#16 libflutter.so +0x946344  dart::Heap::CollectOldSpaceGarbage(...)
#17 libflutter.so +0x93c8c4  dart::Thread::HandleInterrupts(unsigned long)
#18 libflutter.so +0x8bd340  dart::IsolateMessageHandler::HandleMessage(...)
#19 libflutter.so +0x8c2b28  dart::MessageHandler::HandleMessages(...)
#20 libflutter.so +0x8c2978  dart::MessageHandlerTask::Run()
#21 libflutter.so +0x93df08  dart::ThreadPool::Worker::Main(unsigned long)
#22 libflutter.so +0x91e0f8  dart::ThreadStart(void*)
```

This means the `TextureVK` (and its framebuffer/render pass) is destroyed synchronously on a **Dart GC worker thread** during weak-handle finalization, rather than being handed to the Vulkan resource manager / raster thread. When this happens after the Activity has been destroyed, the Mali driver aborts.

A variant with the same Impeller frames also shows `libvulkan.so` on the stack (Galaxy A54, Android 14).

### Affected devices

All ARM Mali GPUs, Android 14–16: Samsung Galaxy A05 (SM-A055F), A06 (SM-A065F), A07 (SM-A075F), A14 (SM-A146P), A54 (SM-A546E), Infinix Hot 50 (X6725), Infinix X6711, Xiaomi 25028RN03A, moto g06, Huawei NLA-LX2P, vivo V2344, C59 Pro.

### Related (already fixed, for context)

On Android 10 devices using the Impeller GLES backend, the same app also hit an abort in `Image.toByteData()` → `DoConvertImageToRasterImpeller` → `BlitPassGLES::EncodeCommands` → `ReactorGLES::AddOperation`. That looks like the bug fixed by flutter/flutter#175102 (shipped in 3.38), so it is not part of this report.

### Code sample

There is no minimal repro yet. What triggers it is holding cloned `ui.Image` handles and letting them be garbage-collected after the Activity is destroyed. We can test a candidate fix or a debug build if that helps.

### Flutter Doctor output

```

Engine • revision 035316565a
```

title: [iOS] Engine artifacts store Flutter.framework/ as 0700; with openrsync (macOS 15.4+) the copy's --chmod is ignored, so flutter build ios embeds an owner-only Flutter.framework
body:
> **Update 2026-10-25:** the on-device consequence I first described as expected turned out not to happen when tested (details under "Actual results"). The artifact modes and the ignored `--chmod` are verified; the severity is lower than first stated.

### Steps to reproduce

On a Mac running macOS 15.4 or later (where `/usr/bin/rsync` is Apple's openrsync), with Flutter 3.47.5 stable (engine `af7e796e16`):

1. `flutter create perms_app && cd perms_app`
2. `flutter build ios --release --no-codesign`
3. `ls -ld build/ios/iphoneos/Runner.app/Frameworks/Flutter.framework`

Also, to see where the mode comes from:

4. `ls -ld "$(flutter --version --machine | python3 -c 'import json,sys;print(json.load(sys.stdin)["flutterRoot"])')"/bin/cache/artifacts/engine/ios-release/Flutter.xcframework/ios-arm64/Flutter.framework`
5. Download `https://storage.googleapis.com/flutter_infra_release/flutter/af7e796e161ae0bb1ff0758c71a7105418bd9ded/ios-release/artifacts.zip` and run `zipinfo artifacts.zip | grep 'Flutter.framework/$'`

### Expected results

`Flutter.framework` inside `Runner.app/Frameworks` is world-readable (`drwxr-xr-x`), as every other folder in the bundle is, so the app bundle works wherever it is installed from.

### Actual results

The embedded framework folder is owner-only:

```
drwx------  9 user  staff  288 Oct 24 14:27 build/ios/iphoneos/Runner.app/Frameworks/Flutter.framework
```

The mode is not introduced by the build; it is in the engine artifacts themselves. Every `Flutter.framework/` directory in `ios-release/artifacts.zip` is stored as `drwx------` while its parents are `drwxr-xr-x`:

```
$ zipinfo artifacts.zip | grep -E 'Flutter\.framework/$|ios-arm64/$|Flutter\.xcframework/$'
drwxr-xr-x  3.0 unx        0 bx stor 26-Sep-17 00:06 extension_safe/Flutter.xcframework/
drwx------  3.0 unx        0 bx stor 26-Sep-17 00:06 extension_safe/Flutter.xcframework/ios-arm64_x86_64-simulator/Flutter.framework/
drwxr-xr-x  3.0 unx        0 bx stor 26-Sep-17 00:05 extension_safe/Flutter.xcframework/ios-arm64/
drwx------  3.0 unx        0 bx stor 26-Sep-17 00:06 extension_safe/Flutter.xcframework/ios-arm64/Flutter.framework/
drwxr-xr-x  3.0 unx        0 bx stor 26-Sep-17 00:06 Flutter.xcframework/
drwx------  3.0 unx        0 bx stor 26-Sep-17 00:06 Flutter.xcframework/ios-arm64_x86_64-simulator/Flutter.framework/
```

`unzip` keeps that mode, so the SDK cache has it for every slice of `ios`, `ios-profile` and `ios-release`:

```
drwx------  ios/Flutter.xcframework/ios-arm64/Flutter.framework
drwx------  ios/Flutter.xcframework/ios-arm64_x86_64-simulator/Flutter.framework
drwx------  ios-profile/Flutter.xcframework/ios-arm64/Flutter.framework
drwx------  ios-profile/Flutter.xcframework/ios-arm64_x86_64-simulator/Flutter.framework
drwx------  ios-release/Flutter.xcframework/ios-arm64/Flutter.framework
drwx------  ios-release/Flutter.xcframework/ios-arm64_x86_64-simulator/Flutter.framework
```

`UnpackIOS` (`copyFramework` in `build_system/targets/darwin.dart`) copies it into `BUILT_PRODUCTS_DIR` with `rsync -av --delete --chmod=Du=rwx,Dgo=rx,Fu=rw,Fgo=r`. On macOS 15.4+ `/usr/bin/rsync` is openrsync, which accepts `--chmod` and does not apply it (#189645 describes the same silent no-op from the read-only-SDK angle). So `BUILT_PRODUCTS_DIR/Flutter.framework` stays `drwx------`, and `xcode_backend.sh embed_and_thin` (`rsync -av`) carries that mode into `Runner.app/Frameworks`.

`xcodebuild archive` hides this: the install step applies `INSTALL_MODE_FLAG = u+w,go-w,a+rX`, so an archive (and therefore `flutter build ipa` and Xcode's Archive) comes out `drwxr-xr-x`. Anything that packages or installs the output of `flutter build ios` directly does not get that correction.

**Tested on a device (2026-10-25):** a release build whose embedded `Flutter.framework/` was `drwx------` (set after the build; the code signature does not seal folder modes) was installed on an iPhone 18 Pro, iOS 27.0.1, with `xcrun devicectl device install app` and launched without a debugger. It launched normally, wrote no crash report and reached its backend. So the owner-only mode does **not** stop an installed app from loading the framework, at least through that install path. This report is therefore a permissions inconsistency in the artifacts plus a silently ineffective `--chmod` (the same no-op #189645 describes from the read-only-SDK side), not a launch failure.

### Suggested fix

- Store `Flutter.framework/` as `0755` in the engine artifacts (the parents already are).
- Since `--chmod` cannot be relied on with openrsync, set the mode explicitly after the copy in `copyFramework` and in `embed_and_thin` (`chmod -R a+rX` on the destination), as #148580 intended.

### Code sample

A plain `flutter create` app is enough; no Dart code is involved.

### Screenshots or Video

None.

### Logs

```

$ sw_vers -productVersion

$ ls -ld build/ios/Release-iphoneos/Flutter.framework build/ios/iphoneos/Runner.app/Frameworks/Flutter.framework

drwx------  9 user  staff  288 Oct 24 14:27 build/ios/iphoneos/Runner.app/Frameworks/Flutter.framework
```

title: Add direct unit tests for MouseCursorManager (services)
body:
`packages/flutter/lib/src/services/mouse_cursor.dart` defines `MouseCursorManager`, the class that implements the cursor candidate resolution protocol used by `MouseTracker`. It has no dedicated test file: searching the test tree, the class is only exercised indirectly via `MouseTracker`-based tests (e.g. `rendering/mouse_tracker_test.dart`, `widgets/mouse_region_test.dart`).

The manager's specified behavior would benefit from direct unit tests that lock it down without a running tracker or a widget tree:

* `MouseCursor.defer` is rejected as the fallback cursor.
* The first non-deferred candidate is selected; empty or all-deferred candidate lists fall back.
* Re-resolving an already-active cursor is a no-op, with or without a triggering `PointerEvent`.
* When the cursor changes, the old session is disposed before the new session is activated.
* Devices are tracked independently; a cursor can hold sessions on multiple devices at once.
* `PointerRemovedEvent` clears the bookkeeping for a device without disposing its session.
* `debugDeviceActiveCursor` returns the last activated cursor and null for unknown devices.

I have a patch ready that adds `packages/flutter/test/services/mouse_cursor_test.dart` covering the above.

title: [tool] build ios-framework keeps a Generated.xcconfig written by a different Flutter SDK
body:
### Steps to reproduce

1. `flutter create -t module m && cd m` (any Flutter SDK).
2. Delete `.ios/Flutter/Generated.xcconfig`, then run `flutter pub get` with SDK A. The file now has `FLUTTER_ROOT=<SDK A>`.
3. Run `flutter build ios-framework` with a different SDK, SDK B.

### Expected results

The build uses SDK B. Afterwards `.ios/Flutter/Generated.xcconfig` names SDK B, as it does after `flutter build ios`.

### Actual results

The file still names SDK A. The build's `pod install` step reads `FLUTTER_ROOT` from it, so it runs against SDK A. If SDK A has no iOS engine artifacts, the build fails:

```
<SDK A>/bin/cache/artifacts/engine/ios/Flutter.xcframework must exist
```

If SDK A does have them, the plugin frameworks build against SDK A's engine.

The cause: `build ios-framework` regenerates `Generated.xcconfig` only through `_updateGeneratedXcodeConfigIfNeeded`, which skips the file when it is newer than the running SDK's `bin/cache/flutter_tools.stamp`. `flutter build ios` and `build ipa` call `updateGeneratedXcodeProperties` on every build (in `buildXcodeProject`), so they don't have this problem.

In practice, SDK A is usually an IDE running `pub get` with a different SDK than the one used on the command line.

### Flutter Doctor output

Not doctor-dependent. Reproduced on macOS with a build of the tool based on the current stable release. The code is the same on master at 66b3ad9017, and a hermetic test against master shows the same behavior (it's in the linked PR).

flutter build ios-framework fails to find the code-signing identity on a module without .ios/
body:
### Steps to reproduce

1. `flutter create -t module mod && cd mod`
2. `rm -rf .ios` (it's generated and usually gitignored, so this is what a fresh CI checkout looks like)
3. `FLUTTER_XCODE_DEVELOPMENT_TEAM=<your team> flutter build ios-framework --no-debug --no-profile`

(With exactly one Apple Development identity for that team in the keychain.)

### Expected results

The frameworks build and are signed with the team's identity, which is what happens if you run step 3 a second time.

### Actual results

```
Finding code-signing identities...
No valid code-signing identity found. Please specify which identity to use with --codesign-identity or use --no-codesign.
```

Since #183399, `BuildIOSFrameworkCommand.runCommand` looks up the code-signing identity (which reads `DEVELOPMENT_TEAM` from `.ios/Runner.xcodeproj` via `xcodebuild -showBuildSettings`) before the build loop calls `regeneratePlatformSpecificToolingIfApplicable`, which is what creates `.ios/` for a module. On a fresh checkout the project doesn't exist yet when it is read, so no team is found. The first run fails, and later runs succeed because the failed run left `.ios/` behind.

### Flutter Doctor output

Reproduced on macOS with Xcode installed, using a 3.47 build of the tool (Shorebird's fork, whose `build_ios_framework.dart` has this same order). `master`'s `runCommand` has the same order.
